title: reqctl_batch_claim.py uses unstable positional batch_index values that drift when earlier batches release, causing later batches to be silently skipped
summary: Caught live while claiming the second batch of the stage-16 requirement-batch loop (after batch 0, DDL-05/MIG-01/MIG-02/MIG-03, completed and was released as DONE). 'python tools/reqctl_batch_claim.py r-co-1-loop --stage "16"' returned batch_index=1 with requirement_ids=['DDL-02','ORD-01','ORD-02','ORD-04'] -- but the ORIGINAL, pre-computed 11-batch plan (independently derived and stated up front by the orchestrating task, and re-confirmed via a fresh 'python tools/reqctl_batch_plan.py --status DRAFT --stage "16" --json' run immediately before claiming) has batch position 2 (1-indexed) / index 1 (0-indexed) in the ORIGINAL numbering as DDL-01/MIG-04/MIG-05/MIG-06, not DDL-02/ORD-01/ORD-02/ORD-04. A fresh, independent re-run of reqctl_batch_plan.py at the moment of the claim confirmed its own index 0 is DDL-01/MIG-04/MIG-05/MIG-06 -- meaning that content had silently become unreachable: the claim tool's own 'done_indices' bookkeeping treats index 0 as permanently DONE (correct in isolation, since MY batch 0 used index 0), but a FRESH recompute of the plan after batch 0's requirements moved to RELEASED status produces a DIFFERENT batch at index 0 (DDL-01/MIG-04/MIG-05/MIG-06, since DDL-05/MIG-01/02/03 are no longer DRAFT and dropped out of the list, shifting every subsequent requirement's batch position down by one). The claim tool then skipped straight to its own index 1, which in the fresh numbering is DDL-02/ORD-01/ORD-02/ORD-04 -- silently orphaning DDL-01/MIG-04/MIG-05/MIG-06 forever, since no future claim call would ever reach index 0 again (it is permanently marked DONE) and the tool has no mechanism to detect that the CONTENT at a given index changed between the plan that marked it DONE and the plan being enumerated now.

root_cause.details: tools/reqctl_batch_claim.py's main() calls reqctl_batch_plan.build_plan() FRESH on every invocation (correctly, per its own comment: 'requirement status changes as you complete batches'), then does 'for idx, batch_ids in enumerate(batches): if idx in done_indices: continue' -- treating the bare positional index from THIS call's fresh enumerate() as if it were the same identifier as the index recorded in handoffs/batch_queue.json's done_indices from a PRIOR call's enumerate() over a DIFFERENT (smaller, since more requirements are still DRAFT at any earlier point) list. build_plan()'s output is a function of the current DRAFT requirement set, which shrinks by design every time a batch releases -- so the requirement set at position N necessarily shifts on every single release. There is no requirement-set-independent identity for a 'batch' anywhere in this design; the position in a list is being used as if it were one. This class of bug (identity conflated with a positional index over a mutating collection) produced exactly one visible symptom here -- one workspace, one release, one immediate re-claim -- but would silently and cumulatively skip MORE requirement batches with every additional release in the same stage, worsening over the life of an 11-batch loop, and would be effectively undetectable after the fact without an independent plan snapshot to compare against (which this run only had because the orchestrating task's instructions had independently pre-stated the full batch plan).

resolution: Two-stage resolution. STAGE 1 (2026-08-11T07:36:37Z): caught before any implementation work started on the wrongly-claimed content; manually corrected handoffs/batch_queue.json's batch_index=1 entry's requirement_ids from ['DDL-02','ORD-01','ORD-02','ORD-04'] to the correct ['DDL-01','MIG-04','MIG-05','MIG-06'] -- a data-level correction only, tool defect left open. STAGE 2 (2026-08-11T09:31:31Z, WF03-GH705-20260811): fixed at the source. tools/reqctl_batch_claim.py now derives a content-stable batch_key(requirement_ids) (sha256 of the sorted, comma-joined requirement IDs, first 12 hex chars) and matches claimed/done state against that key instead of the positional batch_index from build_plan()'s freshly-recomputed list. batch_index is retained in queue entries as an informational display ordinal only -- it is never used for claim/skip matching. tools/reqctl_batch_release.py was given the same fix: it now accepts a batch_key selector (preferred, matches what reqctl_batch_claim.py prints) and falls back to the legacy positional batch_index only for backward compatibility, with an explicit docstring warning that the positional form is not reliable across separate build_plan() calls. The existing handoffs/batch_queue.json entries (batch 0 DONE, batch 1 IN_PROGRESS/r-co-1-loop) were migrated in place to carry the correct batch_key for their existing content, preserving the paused stage-16 loop's IN_PROGRESS lock exactly as it was.
verification: Re-read docs/requirements.yaml after the correction: DDL-01, MIG-04, MIG-05, MIG-06 all confirmed status=DRAFT. handoffs/batch_queue.json now correctly shows batch_index=1 locked by r-co-1-loop with the intended requirement set, plus its correct batch_key (d5019e857a4f). Verified the fix against a scratch copy of the real queue file: claiming stage 16 with a throwaway workspace ID correctly SKIPPED the IN_PROGRESS batch (content DDL-01/MIG-04/MIG-05/MIG-06, whatever array position it occupies in a fresh build_plan() recompute) and claimed the genuinely-next-unclaimed batch (DDL-02/ORD-01/ORD-02/ORD-04) instead -- exactly the behavior that was missing before. tools/test_reqctl_batch_claim.py (new regression test, 3 cases) passes: batch_key is content-stable and order-independent; the exact reshuffle-after-release scenario from this issue no longer skips or double-claims a batch; and the _queue_sync.py fix (shared with ISS-0666) merges batch_queue.json-shaped items without KeyError. python tools/lint_handoffs.py: 0 BLOCKER, 0 MAJOR after the fix.
prevention: tools/reqctl_batch_claim.py must key queue entries by CONTENT (e.g. a sorted tuple/hash of the requirement_ids a batch actually contains, or a stable requirement-id-derived key) rather than by the position that content happens to occupy in the most recent build_plan() enumeration. A batch's identity must not depend on how many other batches have completed before it.

Alternative fix: compute the FULL plan once up front (before ANY batch in the stage is claimed) and freeze it as an ordered, immutable list keyed by content -- claim/release then operate against that frozen list's stable keys, never re-deriving positions from a shrinking DRAFT set mid-stage.

Add a regression test that claims batch 0, marks it DONE, then asserts a second claim call returns the SAME requirement_ids a plan computed BEFORE batch 0 was released would have called 'batch 1' -- this exact scenario, automated, would have caught this on the very first stage that ever completed more than one batch.

This is a BLOCKER-severity class of bug precisely because it fails silently and cumulatively: every future workspace running the requirement-batch loop on ANY multi-batch stage will skip an increasing number of requirement batches without any error, warning, or detectable symptom short of independently cross-checking the plan by hand, as was done here only because the orchestrating task happened to pre-state the full plan.

This local record is being marked RESOLVED because the immediate data corruption for THIS run was caught and fixed; the underlying tool defect in tools/reqctl_batch_claim.py remains open and is filed as its own follow-up (see linked GitHub issue) since fixing the tool itself is out of scope for a WF-02 requirement-implementation run per the Unblock-Everything/forwarding boundary -- it did not block this run's own completion once corrected by hand.
